method_note: Chose the claims that (a) a deterministic oracle would pin or hard-code (folder, blob, digest, version number, status code, vocabulary version), (b) carry repository metadata (licence, archived, push date), (c) map to an existing engine check, and (d) cite DOIs. Byte-level facts were re-read through read-only gh api (tree listings, blob ids, SHA-256 of raw bytes). Page facts were re-read through WebFetch (summarised, so counted as second-hand where noted). The engine checks were compared with docs/reference/capabilities.md and docs/explanation/architecture.md. No EN/ISO/IEC/DIN text was opened; only an IDTA README line that names EN documents was read.

checked.evidence: The capabilities page describes aas.validate as wrapping a pinned aas-test-engines release and warns that a valid AAS is not a complete DPP conformance statement. checked.correction: Set existing_check to partial: aas.validate gives a generic AAS validity result only. A template-conformance step (compare submodel to the pinned JSON: idShort, semanticId, value types) is a new capability, not just oracle.pin_manifest.

checked.claim_ref: conformance_implications[3] and [4] existing_check = identifier.resolve; new_capability_needed = none
checked.claim: identifier.resolve covers the checks 'accept any 3xx with Location, report observed code' and probing ?linkType=linkset / ?linkType=all.
checked.evidence: identifier.resolve has two parameters (accept, accepted_media_types) and judges the final media type. The transport follows redirects itself and checks each hop; there is no parameter to add a query such as linkType, no parameter to assert an intermediate status code, and no linkset-specific logic. So neither probe is possible with the current check.
checked.correction: Set new_capability_needed to a resolver-behaviour check (query parameters, Accept: application/linkset+json, first-hop status class 3xx, Location header, linkset JSON structure). Keep 'none' only for the loopback fixture.

rule5_findings.problem: No paraphrase of EN content found. The file only says that IDTA documents name EN 18223:2026 and EN 18222:2026 as basis; the IDTA README also lists the other JTC 24 modules, which the file does not repeat. This is bibliographic and acceptable. One small risk: 'EN 18222:2026' as a year-qualified designation is taken from an IDTA text; only EN 18223:2026 carries a year in the README line read here.
rule5_findings.fix: Write 'EN 18222' without the year unless the year is shown in a source read, or cite the README line. Keep url as 'not opened'.

rule5_findings.problem: No rule 5 problem. DIN DKE SPEC 99100 is named only as an alignment statement in the CX-0160 page, with no content.

missed_items.fact: WIP main replaced the last 307 fallback with a 404 that may include a linkset, and adds the Accept header application/linkset+json as an alternative to linkType=linkset. 0.7.0 does not have these. A 3xx-only oracle would therefore mark a WIP-conformant 404 as a failure.
Both versions show 400 for an invalid element string, 404 when no record exists and no redirect is possible, and 200 for a returned linkset. The f04 file names only 307 and one 404 case.

The 1.0.1 README names the change as a fix of one full expanded example; the 1.0.2 README says the machine-readable files were corrected and the PDF is unchanged. The issue numbers fixed in 1.0.2 are 187, 207, 208, 210.
The Technical Guidance PDF sits twice in the Battery Pass repository (docs/1.1 and docs/Battery Pass Deliverables/WP3 ...) with the same blob.
The Digital Battery Passport folder of the IDTA repository also holds a guideline PDF written together with Catena-X, in two files (one with a 1.0.1 suffix). The f04 pin table does not list it.

overall: The byte-level and metadata claims are reliable: every blob id, size, SHA-256, repository licence, archived flag, push date, version folder, release status and Catena-X changelog label that I re-read matched. The weakest parts are the UNTP redirect statement (WIP main does not have five 307 arrows and ends with a 404, so the 'same in both versions' claim is wrong) and the engine mapping, where three existing_check entries (aas.validate, identifier.resolve, data.context) claim more than the capability documents allow. A smaller wording error is the claim that CX-0143 changelog entries 1.3.0 to 1.5.0 all name aspect 6.1.0; only 1.3.0 does. DOIs and years are correct. I found no rule 5 problem. Items not re-checked: the in-file CC BY-NC 4.0 sentence, the 'next' EcoPass KIT page, parts 2 to 4 folder digests, and the ELI redirect code.
